touches.text: PURPOSE: A unit of work or attention, written down so it can be followed.
TICKET is abstract. Every real ticket is one of the kinds below.
The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast), its plan file and its trail (the log beside it).

The abstract Ticket is either a tool or a machine, never a device; harbor_master (5.9) only reports over it. Which of the two is settled by the tool test (Law 6): if it must gate writes at its own address, it is a machine. (Q#3, Akien 2026-10-28: "it's either a tool or a machine.")
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor).
Each workflow step declares what it needs.
Carries its WATCHME spec.
Lives in CairnCommons/tickets/ while staged; its trail migrates beside its code as that component's history while under way, and back to the commons after (Law 5).
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10). The gates are housed in harbor_master.
Inference Ticket: the record of one call to the inference proxy, everything that happened to that request.
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
Task Ticket: work the system needs done that does not change code, eg deploying our environment onto a second computer to use its compute.
harbor_master (machine)

"it owns the gates only because we had to have some place to put them, but it does not control anything." The gates refuse on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10: "the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal.")
VERBS: crossing, watch, clear. clear is the PROVED gate it houses on the ticket's behalf.

Outline check (Akien, 2026-10-26): when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing.
artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). USERS: everyone who writes a record.
charter: compiles a component's bounded state from its history. Held by CodeMother.
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

The crossing is the ticket's own act. The gate's probe (the same kind that sends notice of gate passage) tells the passing ticket "you can now advance to X", and the ticket updates itself. (Q#61, Akien 2026-10-27)
question: the open-question door: a decision only you can make, bound to its ticket, answered in your words. → Ticket (3.3.5)? Operator?
proof_coverage: joins a ticket's falsifier clauses to the proofs that cover them and the seals that ran green. → Tester
ticket_inspector: completeness checks over tickets at rest. → CodeMother
